carousels.name: 5 rules for movies and series when p*rn is your weak spot

slides.title: 5 rules for movies and series [[when p*rn is your weak spot.]]
slides.sub: One scene can undo a good week.

slides.title: Rules [[1–2]]
items: Check before you watch. Look up content warnings first.
Skip the scene. Fast-forward or leave the room — no "just this once."

slides.title: Rules [[3–4]]
items: Watch with people when you can, not alone in bed.
Don't search for the scene afterwards. That's how p*rn sessions start.

slides.title: Know your [[limits]]
slides.body: Some shows are a p*rn trailer with a plot. If a series keeps triggering you, drop it. It's just a show.

slides.title: Before you [[press play]]
items: Check the content advisory online.
Keep the remote in your hand.
Set an end time — no autoplay binges.
Pick something you'd watch with your mum in the room.

slides.title: 4 ways to handle sexual frustration [[without p*rn.]]
slides.sub: Wanting sex is normal. P*rn isn't the only answer.

slides.title: Burn it [[off]]
slides.body: Hard training — sprints, lifting, a long run. Many guys say a hard workout takes the edge off fast.

slides.title: Fix your [[sleep]]
slides.body: Tired brains crave quick rewards like p*rn. A rested brain handles desire better.

slides.title: Build real [[connection]]
slides.body: Frustration often hides loneliness. Time with people — friends, dating, a partner — meets more of what you're actually missing.

slides.title: And [[4: patience]]
items: Desire comes in waves — it passes.
Don't feed it with suggestive scrolling.
Many people say p*rn makes the frustration worse over time.
